entry: Aquatic invertebrate of the [[Phylum|phylum]] Porifera, most of them marine. Sponges are multicellular filter feeders that lack true tissues and organs, drawing water through pores and expelling it through an opening called the osculum. Flagellated choanocyte cells drive the water flow and capture most food. Sponges have no complex nervous, digestive or circulatory systems. Adult sponges are sessile, attached to a surface. Many have a mesh-like skeleton of spicules made of calcium carbonate or silicon dioxide, embedded in spongin, a modified collagen. Demosponges, the most numerous group, include all freshwater sponges. Fossil sponges such as Otavia date to as early as the Tonian period, around 800 Mya. Sponges may be the sister group to all other animals, though the evidence remains inconclusive.

Utensil with a shallow bowl, oval or round, at the end of a handle. Spoons are a type of [[Cutlery|cutlery]], used mainly for transferring food to the mouth and also for measuring, mixing, stirring and serving. Present-day spoons are made of metal, wood, porcelain or plastic. Ancient Egyptians made spoons of ivory, flint, slate and wood, many carved with religious symbols, and in [[Shang dynasty]] China spoons were made of bone. In the early Muslim world, spoons were used for eating soup. The earliest English reference to a spoon appears to be in a will of 1259. The Coronation Spoon, used in the anointing of English and later British sovereigns, dates to the 12th century and is the oldest surviving item in the British royal regalia. A 2024 study identified 241 small, spoon-shaped objects at 116 archaeological sites in Scandinavia, Germany and Poland, dating to the Roman era, which the study proposes were used to administer drugs before battles.

Sexual position and cuddling technique, named for spoons placed side by side with their bowls aligned. As a sex position it is a form of rear-entry position, another form being [[Doggy style|doggy style]], and it has been called one of the "basic four" sex positions. Both partners control the angle and depth of penetration, and the close contact allows cuddling. It may suit people who are pregnant, recovering from illness or surgery, or elderly, because it puts less strain on the muscles and does not press on the abdomen. Visual stimulation is limited because partners do not face each other.

Unit of sexual (in fungi) or asexual reproduction, adapted for dispersal and survival. Spores form part of the life cycles of many [[Plant|plants]], [[Algae|algae]], fungi and protozoa, and were thought to have appeared as early as the mid-late [[Ordovician]] period as an adaptation of early land plants. Bacterial spores are not part of a sexual cycle but are resistant structures that help bacteria survive unfavorable conditions. In plants, spores are usually haploid and unicellular and are produced by meiosis in the sporangium of a diploid [[Sporophyte|sporophyte]]. Under favorable conditions a spore develops by mitosis into a multicellular [[Gametophyte|gametophyte]], which produces gametes. Two gametes fuse to form a zygote that develops into a new sporophyte, a cycle known as alternation of generations. The spores of seed plants are produced internally and form the seeds and pollen grains.

Diploid multicellular phase of the life cycle of a plant or alga. The sporophyte develops from a zygote formed when a haploid egg is fertilized by a haploid sperm, so each of its cells has two sets of chromosomes, one from each parent. It produces spores by meiosis, and these develop into the haploid [[Gametophyte|gametophyte]] phase, which alternates with the sporophyte in all land plants and most multicellular algae. In [[Bryophyte|bryophytes]] such as mosses, liverworts and hornworts, the gametophyte is dominant and the small sporophyte depends on it for nutrition. In seed plants, including [[Gymnosperm|gymnosperms]] and angiosperms, the sporophyte is the more prominent phase and is the familiar plant with roots, stems, leaves and cones or flowers. During the [[Devonian]] period, several plant groups independently evolved heterospory, an early step in the evolution of seeds.

Tools, materials, apparel and gear used in sport, from balls and nets to rackets and protective items such as [[Helmet|helmets]]. Balls are usually spheres, though gridiron football and rugby balls are spheroid or ellipsoid, and in many ball sports they form part of the scoring mechanism. Nets are used in [[Tennis|tennis]], [[Badminton|badminton]] and [[Volleyball|volleyball]], where the ball is struck over a net supported by two posts. Rackets are netted tools for striking balls or shuttlecocks, while paddles are flat-faced tools used in sports such as pickleball and table tennis. Footwear includes cleats, cycling shoes and ski boots. Footballs date back to ancient China, between the [[Warring States period]] (476–221 BC) and the [[Han dynasty|Han Dynasty]] (220 AD), and have changed from animal skin to layers of polyester or cotton. Newer equipment is increasingly electronic and connected, delivering performance data.

Swedish freemium music streaming service, founded in April 2006 in [[Stockholm]] by Daniel Ek and Martin Lorentzon. It offers over 100 million songs, 8 million podcast titles and 800,000 audiobook titles. Basic features are free with advertisements, while offline and commercial-free listening require paid subscriptions. Spotify pays royalties based on each artist's streams as a proportion of total songs streamed, and distributes about 70% of its total revenue to rights holders, often record labels. Its users are based largely in the [[United States]] and Europe. Spotify is listed on the [[New York Stock Exchange]] in the form of American depositary receipts.

Common name for a group of small, oily forage fish of the genus *Sprattus* in the family Clupeidae. Sprats are highly active, schooling fish that swim continuously throughout the day, and they are rich in polyunsaturated fats, considered beneficial to the human diet. They are eaten in many places and are often classed as [[Sardine|sardines]], a broad category. Products sold as anchovies have sometimes been prepared from sprats, as authentic anchovies were once less accessible. The [[Baltic Sea]] is the most studied habitat, where *Sprattus sprattus* forages and reproduces. Sprat numbers there have fluctuated with the availability of zooplankton, and the population has increased dramatically in recent decades. The average time from fertilization to hatching is about 15 days.

Computer application for computation, organization, analysis and storage of data in tabular form. Spreadsheets were developed as computerized analogs of paper accounting worksheets. Each cell may contain numeric or text data, or a formula that calculates a value from other cells, so changing one value updates the results. This makes spreadsheets useful for "what-if" analysis. Several sheets form a workbook. LANPAR, introduced in 1969, was the first electronic spreadsheet on mainframe and time-sharing computers, and VisiCalc (1979) was the first on a microcomputer, becoming the killer application for the [[Apple II]]. [[Microsoft Excel|Excel]] has the largest market share for Windows and Mac. Built-in functions cover [[Standard deviation|standard deviation]] and [[Regression analysis|regression analysis]], along with net present value. Spreadsheets have replaced paper-based systems throughout business.

Period of Chinese history, roughly the first half of the [[Zhou dynasty|Eastern Zhou]], marked by the erosion of royal power. Its name derives from the *Spring and Autumn Annals*, a chronicle of the state of Lu, which tradition associates with [[Confucius]]. Local lords nominally subject to the Zhou gained increasing autonomy, negotiated their own alliances and waged war on one another. In 771 BCE a Quanrong invasion, in coalition with the states of Zeng and Shen, destroyed the Western Zhou capital at Haojing and killed King You, and the Zhou court moved east to Luoyi, where it had real control over only a small royal demesne. Regular conferences of the most important states sometimes declared one vassal ruler hegemon. The partition of Jin by three elite families in 403 BCE is generally considered to mark the end of the period and the start of the [[Warring States period]].

Elastic object, typically of metal, bent or molded to return to shape after being compressed, extended or twisted. The spring constant, or rate, is the change in force divided by the change in deflection, and its inverse is compliance. In 1676 [[Robert Hooke]] postulated [[Hooke's law]], which states that the force a spring exerts is proportional to its extension. Coiled springs appeared early in the 15th century, in door locks, and spring-powered clocks followed. Common types include tension, compression and [[Torque|torsion]] springs, the last producing torque proportional to the angle of twist. Most are made from spring steel, while [[Titanium|titanium]] and phosphor bronze are used where corrosion resistance matters. Simple non-coiled springs, such as the bow, have been used throughout human history.

Natural point where groundwater emerges from an [[Aquifer|aquifer]] and flows across the ground surface as surface water. Springs are part of the [[Hydrosphere|hydrosphere]] and the [[Water cycle|water cycle]], and have long been an important source of fresh water, especially in arid regions. They are driven out by natural forces such as gravity and hydrostatic pressure. Springs form where groundwater reaches the surface, for example where the water table rises above it, or through [[Karst]] topography or volcanic activity. Yields vary from nearly zero to more than 14,000 liters per second (490 cu ft/s) for the largest springs. Artesian springs occur where pressure in a confined aquifer pushes water straight up out of the ground. A [[Hot spring|hot spring]] is fed by geothermally heated groundwater, and a [[Geyser|geyser]] is a hot spring in which trapped superheated groundwater produces recurring eruptions of hot water and steam.

One of the four temperate seasons, between winter and summer. Spring is also known as springtime and denotes rebirth, renewal and regrowth. When it is spring in the Northern Hemisphere, it is autumn in the Southern Hemisphere. At the [[Equinox|spring equinox]], also called the vernal equinox, days and nights are approximately twelve hours long, and daytime length increases until the [[Summer solstice|summer solstice]]. The spring equinox falls in March in the Northern Hemisphere and in September in the Southern Hemisphere. Meteorologists define spring by monthly average temperatures: March, April and May in the United States and United Kingdom, and September, October and November in Australia, New Zealand, South Africa and Brazil. Subtropical and tropical areas are better described by wet and dry seasons. The word derives from the Middle English verb springen, meaning to rise up or burst forth.

Class (Collembola) of small, wingless arthropods, the largest of the three lineages of hexapods that are no longer considered insects. Springtails are omnivorous, free-living organisms that prefer moist conditions, and there are more than 9,000 species worldwide. They contribute indirectly to [[Decomposition|decomposition]] by fragmenting organic matter and controlling soil microbial communities. Most species have a forked appendage, the furcula, folded beneath the body, which snaps against the surface to fling the springtail into the air. Members are normally less than 6 mm long, and some can reduce their body size by as much as 30% through [[Moulting|molting]] when temperatures rise. The name Collembola comes from Greek words for glue and peg, after a tube on the abdomen once thought to stick the creature to surfaces.

Large-scale electrical discharge in the mesosphere, high above [[Thunderstorm|thunderstorm]] clouds. Sprites appear as luminous red-orange flashes, often occurring in clusters at altitudes of 50–90 km. They are usually triggered by positive [[Lightning|lightning]] discharges between an underlying thundercloud and the ground. Although sometimes called upper-atmospheric lightning, they are cold plasma phenomena, more akin to fluorescent tube discharges. The earliest known report dates from 1886, and they were first photographed in 1989 by scientists from the University of Minnesota. Their root cause remains unknown beyond a general association with positive cloud-to-ground lightning.

[[Conifer|Coniferous]] evergreen tree of the genus *Picea* in the pine family, Pinaceae. The genus comprises some 37 species found in the northern temperate and boreal regions of the Northern Hemisphere. Spruce needles are four-sided and attached singly to small peg-like structures that remain on the twigs after the needles fall, a feature that distinguishes spruces from other Pinaceae. Spruce is a major source of construction timber and of pulp for paper, and it is the standard material for the soundboards of stringed instruments such as acoustic [[Guitar|guitars]]. The Norway spruce is widely used for Christmas trees. Spruces generally live 100 to 600 years; the oldest reported age for a single tree is 852 years, for a *Picea engelmannii*. [[Edvard Munch]] depicted spruces around 1900.

First artificial Earth satellite, launched by the [[Soviet Union]] on October 4, 1957. It was a polished metal sphere 58 cm (23 in) in diameter with four external radio antennas, and its radio signal was easily detected by [[Amateur radio|amateur radio]] operators. Its 65° orbital inclination meant its flight path covered virtually the entire inhabited Earth. The success was unanticipated by the United States, which precipitated the American Sputnik crisis and triggered the start of the [[Space Race]]. The transmitter batteries were depleted after 22 days. After 1,440 orbits, Sputnik 1 burned up on reentry on January 4, 1958. Tracking it provided data on the density of the upper atmosphere and on the ionosphere.

Regular quadrilateral with four equal sides and four right angles. A square is a special case of a [[Rhombus|rhombus]] and of a rectangle, and its area is the side length multiplied by itself, which gives the term squaring in algebra. Equal squares tile the plane edge to edge, so square tilings appear in floors, graph paper and image [[Pixel|pixels]]. Squares are the only regular polygons whose internal, central and external angles are all equal, each being a right angle. The diagonals of a square are equal, bisect each other and meet at 90 degrees. Attempts to square the circle with compass and straightedge, which the area formula motivated, are now known to be impossible. Squares can be inscribed in any smooth or convex curve, but it remains unsolved whether a square can be inscribed in every simple closed curve.

Number y whose square, y², equals a given number x. Every nonnegative real number has a unique nonnegative square root, called the principal square root and written √x. For example, 4 and −4 are square roots of 16. Every positive number has two square roots, one positive and one negative. Square roots of negative numbers are discussed within [[Complex number|complex numbers]]. A Babylonian clay tablet dated between 1800 and 1600 BC gives a base-60 value corresponding to 1.41421296 for √2. The Greeks knew that the square roots of positive integers that are not perfect squares are [[Irrational number|irrational]], a theorem almost certainly due to Theaetetus, dating to c. 380 BC.

Racket sport played in a four-walled court with a small, hollow rubber ball. It is played by two players in singles or four in doubles, and the players alternate striking the ball so the opponent cannot make a return. About 20 million people play squash regularly in over 185 countries. The sport derives from the older game of rackets, and a punctured ball that "squashed" against the wall was used at Harrow School around 1830. The first squash court in North America was built at St. Paul's School in Concord, New Hampshire, in 1884. The standard singles court measures 9.75 meters by 6.4 meters. The governing body, World Squash, is recognized by the International Olympic Committee, and squash will be included in the [[Olympic Games]] from the 2028 Summer Olympics in [[Los Angeles]].

Cephalopod mollusc with an elongated soft body, large eyes, eight arms and two long tentacles. Squid have a small internal skeleton, a rod-like gladius or pen, made of [[Chitin|chitin]]. They diverged from other cephalopods during the [[Jurassic]] and became prominent around 100 million years ago, at the boundary between the Early and Late Cretaceous. Squid occupy a role similar to [[Teleost|teleost]] fish as open-water predators, using their two long tentacles to grab prey and their eight arms to hold it. Many swim rapidly by jet propulsion and locate prey by sight. Squid can change color for camouflage and signaling, some species are bioluminescent, and many eject a cloud of ink to distract predators. Groups of Humboldt squid have been observed hunting cooperatively. Squid are preyed on by sharks, fish, seabirds, seals and [[Sperm whale|sperm whales]], and are used in cuisines around the world, often as calamari.

South Korean dystopian survival thriller television series. Created, written and directed by Hwang Dong-hyuk for [[Netflix]], *Squid Game* follows 456 players in financial hardship who risk death in children's games for a prize of ₩45.6 billion (US$34.02 million). Hwang outlined the story in 2009, drawing on class disparity in South Korea and on [[Capitalism|capitalism]]. The first season, released on September 17, 2021, became Netflix's most-watched series and won six Primetime Emmy Awards and a Golden Globe. The second season was released on December 26, 2024, and the third and final season on June 27, 2025. The later seasons were considered inferior to the first.

Member of the rodent family Sciuridae, including tree squirrels, ground squirrels such as [[Chipmunk|chipmunks]] and [[Prairie dog|prairie dogs]], and flying squirrels. Squirrels are indigenous to the Americas, Eurasia and Africa, and were introduced by humans to Australia. The earliest known fossil squirrels date from the [[Eocene]] epoch. They range from the African pygmy squirrel, 10–14 cm long and weighing 12–26 g, to the Bhutan giant flying squirrel, up to 1.27 m long. Most have slender bodies, long bushy tails and large eyes, and tree squirrels can descend a tree headfirst by rotating their ankles 180 degrees. Squirrels live in almost every habitat from tropical [[Rainforest|rainforest]] to semiarid desert. They are predominantly herbivorous, eating seeds and nuts, though many also eat insects. Adults can live 5 to 10 years in the wild. The name derives from Latin sciurus and Ancient Greek skiouros, from words meaning shade and tail.

Genocidal killing of more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys in and around the town of Srebrenica in July 1995, during the [[Bosnian War]]. It was carried out mainly by units of the Bosnian Serb Army of [[Republika Srpska]] under Ratko Mladić. Although the [[United Nations|UN]] had declared Srebrenica a "safe area", a contingent of 370 lightly armed Dutch soldiers failed to deter its capture. The [[International Court of Justice]] ruled in 2007 that the massacre constituted genocide. In 2005 [[Kofi Annan]], then UN Secretary-General, called it "a terrible crime – the worst on European soil since the Second World War."

Indian philosopher, yogi and nationalist. He took part in the movement for Indian independence from British rule, advocating complete autonomy through his writings and political activity, and was involved in the [[Indian National Congress]]. Arrested after bombings linked to a revolutionary group, he faced a public trial for treason in the Alipore Conspiracy and was then released. He withdrew to [[Pondicherry]] to devote himself to spiritual practice and formulated Integral Yoga, set out in *The Life Divine* and *The Synthesis of Yoga*. With Mirra Alfassa he founded the Sri Aurobindo Ashram in 1926. His literary output includes the epic poem *Savitri* and translations and commentaries on the [[Vedas]] and [[Upanishads]].
